scope_note: Verifies the conformance_implications of m01 to m10 against the engine source at commit b290791 in this worktree. Verdict rubric: the existing_check claim is read as written, including its own stated limits, against the test_objective. correct = the named check, with its registered parameters, does what the entry says, or the entry states its limit accurately and names the gap as new_capability_needed, including when the check today gives blocked or unsupported on the objective (so correct does not mean that a verdict is produced today). overstated = the check covers only part of what the entry claims, or the entry says no new capability is needed when one is. wrong = the named check gives no judgment on the objective (blocked, unsupported, a verdict in the wrong direction, or a different observable). check_missing = the entry names a check that is not registered. For existing_check 'none': correct if no registered check covers the objective; wrong if one does. Partial finds for 'none' entries are listed under missed_existing_checks. No web source was retrieved in this task; oracle_sources are source ids carried over from the method files, not re-verified here. No test suite was run.

mapping_checks.reason: The parser accepts only the /01/<GTIN>/21/<serial> path and refuses other URLs with IDENTIFIER.SYNTAX.INVALID; another scheme name gives unsupported. It has no length bound and accepts http as well as https, so the proposed https-url scheme is a real gap.

The transport bounds redirects and checks each hop against the policy, and has no downgrade rule, as the entry says. But a chain over max_redirects ends as too_many_redirects and an oversized body as TRANSPORT.BODY_TRUNCATED, both inconclusive (unreachable or blocked), never a fail. The bound is enforced, not judged.
Compares the carrier text with the top-level key 'id' of the resolved passport and with a declared sample identifier. The registration-identifier half is correctly left to a new capability.
carrier.qr_decode covers the decode only (one readable QR symbol). 'Leads to the battery passport' needs identifier.resolve as a second step, which the entry does not name.
manual.review verifies a signed manual result bound to the test purpose and the SUT; the engine does not perform the review, which fits process evidence.

For a role with an entitled path, a 401 or 403 on the fetch channel fails with ACCESS.ENTITLEMENT.REFUSED, and each entitled path must be at the root of the fetch body. Needs the law-derived policy file the entry names.

The check reads at most five channel kinds (fetch, export, search, error, html), one path template each, under the 'api' endpoint. 'Any channel' is broader than that closed set; leaks through other endpoints are not probed.

data.rules has five rule kinds: required_fields, unit, range, relationship, freshness. There is no pattern rule and no rule that asserts a field is absent, so it cannot test 'stores no personal data'.
No check records cookies or third-party fetches. Set-Cookie values are replaced with a removal marker in records, and HTML is never rendered.

A rule's 'when' condition reads only ICS and profile facts. Category conditions work; date conditions do not, because the evaluation date is not a fact. A date-conditional rule pack is not possible without a change to applicability facts.
Validates the item or model document against the schema that the profile pins. The entry correctly says no Commission schema exists yet and proposes pinning it.
The 'unit' rule kind tests that a value is in an allowed set at a dotted path, which works as an enumeration check for a scalar field (not inside arrays).
required_fields checks presence. The document is fetched for the anonymous role, so presence means presence in the public view. Fields inside arrays cannot be addressed.
data.rules has no structural or absence rule, so it cannot express 'voluntary data is separate'. Only the manual.review branch applies.

proposed_capabilities.purpose: Let data.jsonschema, data.context and data.rules judge a named sample artifact or a further resource (registry record, message, linkset), not only the item or model document fetched over HTTP.
proposed_capabilities.observable: Bytes of an IXIT sample or of a declared resource, parsed as strict JSON.
proposed_capabilities.dependencies_or_licences: None. Contract change to report: DocumentKind (src/dppce/adapters/data.py:39) is adapter-owned, but a resource other than item|model needs ResourceName in src/dppce/models/declarations.py:22 (protected).

proposed_capabilities.purpose: Extend rule packs with pattern, forbidden-field, string-equality and array (any or all element) rules, and with the evaluation date as a fact for 'when' conditions.
proposed_capabilities.observable: Values at dotted paths, including list elements, of the judged document.
proposed_capabilities.dependencies_or_licences: None (re in the standard library). The rule-pack schema dppce.rulepack/1 needs a new version. An evaluation-date fact changes facts_from in src/dppce/applicability.py:32 (protected): report it. A personal-data rule stays a heuristic: absence of a pattern does not prove absence of personal data.

proposed_capabilities.purpose: Turn a published schema set into a reviewed, offline, digest-pinned bundle: rewrite absolute $ref values to local pointers and convert draft-04 keywords to 2020-12.
proposed_capabilities.observable: The pinned schema files; the result is input to data.jsonschema.
proposed_capabilities.dependencies_or_licences: None; jsonschema and referencing are installed. This is a maintainer tool with a review step, not a run-time fetch. Licence of each imported schema set must be recorded per bundle (not checked in this session).

proposed_capabilities.purpose: Pin a snapshot of the Commission semantic repository data models and metadata as local files and validate passports against it.
proposed_capabilities.observable: Passport document against the pinned model snapshot.
proposed_capabilities.dependencies_or_licences: Unknown until the Commission publishes the format; if it is SHACL or OWL it depends on data.shacl.

observations: Every check named in an existing_check field is registered (14 checks in src/dppce/testdefs/registry.py via the adapters); no entry names an unregistered check, so check_missing is 0.

Biggest systemic gap: data.jsonschema, data.context and data.rules read only the item or model document, fetched over HTTP (src/dppce/adapters/data.py:39, 113-129). They have no sample-artifact input. Many entries label these checks 'sample-artifact'; for a passport that the SUT serves this is only a wrong label, but for messages, registration files, registry records, offers and descriptors the check cannot run. Proposed: data.document_source (S).

data.rules has five rule kinds and no pattern, absence, string-equality or list rule; dotted paths do not enter arrays (src/dppce/adapters/common.py:334). The relationship rule compares numbers only. Several entries that say 'new capability: none' with data.rules rely on rules that do not exist. Rule 'when' conditions read ICS and profile facts only, not the evaluation date (src/dppce/applicability.py:32). Proposed: data.rule_kinds.

identifier.resolve judges 404 and 410 as IDENTIFIER.UNRESOLVED and any other non-200 status as a fail (src/dppce/adapters/identifier.py:194-204). For resolver-conformance tests where 400 or 404 is the expected answer, the check gives the opposite verdict, so it cannot be the oracle for error behaviour.

Hop URLs of a redirect chain are recorded in Record.redirects (src/dppce/infrastructure/transport.py:481); per-hop status codes and headers are not. Response header values other than a fixed safe list are replaced with a removal marker, including CORS headers, Set-Cookie, and Link values whose relation is not on a fixed list (src/dppce/infrastructure/redaction.py:22-111). Resolver, CORS, cookie and Link-header capabilities need infrastructure changes, not only adapter code.

integrity.jws verifies one profile: ES256, typ dpp+jws, key from an x5c chain, headers alg, kid, typ, x5c only (src/dppce/evidence/jws.py:27-29; src/dppce/adapters/integrity.py:41, 160). Any other JWS profile gives blocked, never a partial signature finding. The allowlist is shared with the engine's own report signing, so a new verification profile must not widen it.

aas.validate parses the sample as strict JSON before it calls check_json_data (src/dppce/adapters/lifecycle.py:181-186). An XML or AASX sample gives AAS.INVALID, a completed fail, not unsupported. This is a rule-7 concern (an unassessed input reads as a defect of the SUT) independent of the method research; reported, not fixed.

Library facts probed in the repository environment (/Users/aeroshariati/DPP-CE/.venv, the worktree has no venv): aas-test-engines 1.0.3 reports file version 3.0 only and has check_xml_data, check_aasx_file and an API mode with four SSP-002 read profiles for 3.0; zxing-cpp 3.1.1 exposes DataMatrix, EAN13, UPCA and symbology_identifier; cryptography provides CMAC; pyshacl, rdflib, pyld, cbor2, pycose, schemathesis, multiformats, lxml and web3 are not installed.

registry.consistency compares exactly two hard-coded field pairs (src/dppce/adapters/lifecycle.py:135-141); persistence.versions applies a fixed rule to an engine-specific listing format and reads no declaration (lifecycle.py:53-78); identifier.consistency reads the top-level key 'id' only (identifier.py:262). Entries that rely on more fields, declared rules, or other identifier locations are overstated.

access.restricted_fields requires a 401 or 403 nowhere: a refusal is a failure only for a role with entitled paths, and a role with no entitled path is judged on leaks only (src/dppce/adapters/access.py:297-305). Channel kinds are a closed set of five with one template each (access.py:41); credentials are sent only as Authorization Bearer (transport.py:371).

The resource names are a closed Literal in a protected model file (src/dppce/models/declarations.py:22). Proposals that target /description, /.well-known paths, version metadata, back-up copies or linksets need that contract change; it is collected as api.resources. ICS.identifier_scheme is a free string (declarations.py:56), so new identifier schemes are adapter changes, and ICS.granularity already exists.
existing_capability fields of m02#29 and m05#22 name a check (carrier.qr_decode), not a capability (carrier.qr).

m10#1: the objective (report a non-GS1 identifier as unsupported, not as a syntax failure) is met today when the ICS declares that scheme (identifier.py:124-126); the pluggable list is needed only for several schemes in one ICS.

m04#2 and m04#6 report probe results dated 2026-10-19. The code paths they describe were verified here (validator() returns None for a non-local $ref; SchemaError maps to DATA.SCHEMA.MALFORMED); the probes themselves were not re-run.

oracle_sources are source ids carried over from the method files m01 to m10 (and checked to exist there or in catalogue/sources.yaml). No source was retrieved or re-verified in this task. Ids of EN, ISO, IEC and DIN documents were left out of oracle_sources even where a method file cites them (rule 5).
Sizes are estimates from reading the code, not measurements. No test suite and no lint were run (task instruction). No source or method file was edited; only this result file was written.
